newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares ease, off lows in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares ease, off lows in thin trade.

text.p: Istanbul shares slipped 0.84 percent lower in depressed and narrow trade on Monday amid persistant cash shortage and negative sentiment, but regained part of the early losses on minor selective buys, brokers said.
The IMKB-100 closed at 62,904.83, down 534.01 points from Friday after moving between 62,618 and 63,438.
Trade volume plunged to 3.4 trillion lira ($38.6 million), nearing the 1996 low of 2.7 trillion ($30.8 million) on July 30, after Friday's 5.6 trillion ($64.5 million).
"The index has firm support at 62,500. It did not fall much although negative developments undermining the market follow one another," said Haydar Haydaroglu from Halkbank.

The market was unnerved by weekend incidents in Cyprus and ongoing fighting in northern Iraq as well as international opposition, particularly from Arab countries to a Turkish plan to set up a security zone there to prevent infiltrations by Kurdish rebels.
Brokers said a strong dollar also discouraged market players.
